findings.title: Unparenthesized OR clauses in SQL conditions break operator precedence when combined with AND
findings.body: `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition`, and `buildFilterConditions` (when only `eventTypeId` is provided) return top-level `OR` SQL fragments without outer parentheses (e.g., `(("teamId" = ...) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)) OR (("userId" = ...) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false))`). When `filterConditions` is `null`, `getBaseConditions()` returns `authConditions` directly without wrapping it in parentheses. Because `AND` binds tighter than `OR` in SQL, embedding `${baseConditions}` (or `${authConditions}` / `${filterConditions}`) into a raw query with additional predicates—such as `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" >= ...`—causes PostgreSQL to parse the condition as `A OR (B AND "startTime" >= ...)`, so one branch of the `OR` completely ignores the remaining `WHERE` filters. Additionally, the `else if (filterConditions)` branch on lines 76-77 would return `filterConditions` without any authorization constraint if `authConditions` were ever falsy; `getBaseConditions()` should always enforce `authConditions` and wrap compound `OR` conditions in parentheses.

findings.title: Caching tests for authorization and filter conditions were removed
findings.body: `InsightsBookingService` still caches `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` in `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()`, but the entire `describe("Caching", ...)` test block was deleted rather than updated for the `Prisma.sql` return values, leaving the caching behavior untested.
